title: Homework
description: YAML front matter of course/assessments/homework/HW0N.md — one homework, spanning one or more units (homework module, HW-D01). One file holds the whole homework, as unit.md holds a unit: its settings, its plan (`plan`, written by /class-kit:plan-homework), the items it was built from (`items`, `versions[].items`, `item_tools`, written by /class-kit:build-homework) and the teacher's approval (`approved`). The items themselves live in the shared bank, course/assessments/items/, and are referenced, not copied.

accepted.description: The teacher's deliberate exceptions for THIS file (D-037). Each entry suppresses one validation rule's findings for this file; `classkit validate` still counts them, so they are never invisible. Only the teacher adds these — an agent never does so on its own.

rule.description: The rule code, as `classkit validate` prints it in brackets, e.g. 'in_class_missing'. Not pattern-checked on purpose: a mistyped code is reported by the advisory rule `unknown_rule`, never as a schema error (D-038).

id.description: Optional (D-048): the one item this exception covers — an objective (U01-O3), a guiding question (U01-S02-G1), an activity (U01-A1), an assessment item (U01-I01), a unit (U03) or a material locator (M0007#slide-3). Without it, the exception covers the rule's findings for the whole file. An id that matches nothing is counted with the stale entries.

reason.description: Why the departure is deliberate, e.g. 'holiday week — no class meeting'. Optional: a missing reason is reported by the advisory rule `accepted_without_reason`, never as a schema error (D-038).

id.description: e.g. 'HW01'. The file is named after it (HW01.md). Not per unit — a homework spans units.

units.description: Units this homework assesses. Every referenced item's `unit` must be one of these (rule `homework_units_declared`).

total_minutes.description: The time budget for a student. `homework_budget_fits` warns when the items' minutes (an item's `est_minutes`, or its class's `typical_minutes` midpoint) drift outside the tolerance.

due_date.description: Due date (YYYY-MM-DD), asked per homework and printed on the student document in the course's `due_date_format` (HW-D30). Optional.

ref.description: For `kind: quiz_report`: the unit whose entry quiz the report is about, e.g. 'U03'.

source.description: Where the homework comes from: `material` — the units' material; `quiz_report` — a unit's entry quiz report, given in the session and never stored (HW-D33). For a quiz report, `ref` is the unit whose entry quiz it reports on (e.g. 'U03'); `homework_source_quiz_exists` checks that unit has entry-quiz items.

allowed_tools.description: The homework's tool policy: tools from `course.yaml`'s `tools` map (HW-D03); `homework_tools_declared` reports a tool that is not declared there.

plan.description: The plan, written by /class-kit:plan-homework and approved at its gate (`classkit approve homework N --stage planned`). The coverage skeleton the build writes items from. Never printed in the students' or the teacher's documents.

focus_notes.description: The teacher's guidance for this homework ('focus on hashing'). No student data (HW-D31).

quiz_summary.description: For a quiz-report homework: only the aggregated figures the plan used ('U03-S02-G2: 38% correct'), and the misconceptions the teacher chose (HW-D34). Never names, identifiers, grades or per-student answers (HW-D33).

slot.description: The slot's number, unique in the plan; the teacher edits slots by number ('slot 2 harder').

guiding_questions.description: What the item will test (`homework_plan_reference` checks they exist).

intent.description: One line: what the item is for — 'remediate the O(1) vs worst-case misconception', not 'assess hashing'.

est_minutes.description: Optional for a class with `time_variance: high`: its `typical_minutes` midpoint is used instead (HW-D06).

tools.description: Tools this item needs (HW-D28), from `course.yaml`'s `tools`; the build copies them into `item_tools`.

decision.description: fresh — a new item; reuse — an existing item, unchanged; adapt — a new item made from an existing one (with `source_ref`). Default: fresh.

from.description: For reuse or adapt: the existing item.

version.description: A version label from `versions`, when the slot belongs to one; absent — a shared slot.

item.description: The item built for this slot — written by /class-kit:build-homework.

slots.description: One slot per item to build. Empty in a scaffolded placeholder.

versions.description: Targeted versions (HW-D26), planned from a quiz report. Every student gets the shared `items` plus their version's `items`. Labels never identify students; which student gets which version stays outside the repository. Checked by `homework_version_reference` and `homework_versions_targeted`.

label.description: Unique within the homework (e.g. 'A', 'gq1-2'). Never a student name or identifier.

targets.description: Guiding Questions this version remediates. Must belong to the homework's declared `units`; each must be tested by at least one of this version's items.

items.description: The version's own items, written by /class-kit:build-homework. Each must test at least one of this version's `targets` and no Guiding Question outside them. An item may appear in several versions.

The shared items, in order — every student gets them. Empty until /class-kit:build-homework writes them. Items are referenced, not copied; each should carry `homework` in its `usage` (rule `homework_item_usage`).

item_tools.description: Tools a specific item needs (HW-D28), keyed by item id: e.g. {U03-I05: [wireshark, gns3]}. Written by /class-kit:build-homework from the plan's slots. Several tools per item are allowed; a programming language counts as a tool. Every tool must be declared in `course.yaml`'s `tools` map (`homework_tools_declared`); every key must be an item of this homework (`homework_item_reference`).

approved.description: The teacher's approval of this homework (spec §8.9) — written by `classkit approve homework N`, or by hand (then usually without `hash`). Editing afterwards is normal and un-approves nothing; `classkit status` uses the hash to say 'edited since'. Agents never write or change it.

stage.description: `planned` — the plan was approved (/class-kit:plan-homework); the hash is over this file without what the build writes (`items`, `versions[].items`, `item_tools`, the slots' `item`). `built` — the whole homework was approved (/class-kit:build-homework); the hash is over this file and every item it lists.

hash.description: sha256 at approval, without this block (spec §8.9). Written by the tool; absent when approved by hand.
